headline: US FDA clears first generic Flovent HFA asthma inhaler, made by Cipla and sold by Teva
dek: The FDA has cleared the first generic of Flovent HFA in 110 mcg and 220 mcg strengths, and Cipla said the US launch has begun.
body:
The US Food and Drug Administration has cleared the first generic version of Flovent HFA, a fluticasone inhaler for asthma, in the 110 mcg and 220 mcg strengths, according to a post on X by The Krish Report that cites a Cipla filing to the NSE and BSE dated 25 November.

The post said Cipla told the exchanges that the launch has already started. It described the product as a joint Cipla and Teva effort: Cipla makes and supplies the inhaler, while Teva holds the US approval and handles sales.

The author wrote that this arrangement gives Cipla the manufacturing side of a first-generic launch, and that the split of revenue with Teva will determine how much of the product reaches Cipla's reported figures. The post cited IQVIA as putting the US market for the two strengths at about $350 million, roughly ₹3,250 crore at current exchange rates.

The author argued that inhalers are difficult to copy, so a first generic can usually expect to have the market largely to itself for a period. The post also said Cipla describes itself as the number two company by prescriptions in US generic respules and inhalers.

Among the risks, the author listed the possibility that further generic approvals could bring prices down quickly. The post also noted that the terms of the Teva arrangement are not public.
key_quote: The US FDA has cleared the first generic version of Flovent HFA, a fluticasone inhaler for asthma, in the 110 mcg and 220 mcg strengths.
